classified_spans.text:
## System Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Agents[Agent Execution Domains]
        A1[LPAR Agent]
        A2[Container Agent]
        A3[Address Space Agent]
        A4[AI Accelerator Agent]
    end

    subgraph Fabric[Zero-Trust Agent Fabric]
        GW[Communication Gateway]
        TE[Trust Evaluator]
        SC[Security Challenge Engine]
        TS[Trust Score Calculator]
        PE[Policy Enforcer]
    end

    subgraph Context[Security Context Sources]
        RACF[RACF Permissions]
        WC[Workload Classifications]
        DSL[Data Sensitivity Labels]
        RA[Runtime Attestations]
    end

    subgraph Actions[Enforcement Actions]
        ALLOW[Allow Communication]
        RESTRICT[Restrict Scope]
        QUARANTINE[Quarantine Agent]
        DENY[Deny Communication]
    end

    subgraph Audit[Audit Trail]
        TDL[Trust Decision Log]
        IL[Interaction Log]
    end

    A1 & A2 & A3 & A4 --> GW
    GW --> TE
    RACF & WC & DSL & RA --> TE
    TE --> SC
    SC --> TS
    TS --> PE
    PE --> ALLOW
    PE --> RESTRICT
    PE --> QUARANTINE
    PE --> DENY
    PE --> TDL
    GW --> IL
```

## Sequence Diagram

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A1 as Requesting Agent
    participant GW as Fabric Gateway
    participant TE as Trust Evaluator
    participant RACF as RACF / Context Sources
    participant SC as Challenge Engine
    participant PE as Policy Enforcer
    participant A2 as Target Agent
    participant AL as Audit Log

    A1->>GW: Invoke Target Agent
    GW->>TE: Evaluate Security Context
    TE->>RACF: Query Permissions and Labels
    RACF-->>TE: Identity, Workload, Sensitivity
    TE->>SC: Issue Security Challenge
    SC->>A1: Validate Identity and Environment
    A1-->>SC: Challenge Response
    SC->>TE: Attestation Result
    TE->>PE: Submit Trust Score
    alt Trust Score Sufficient
        PE->>A2: Forward Invocation
        A2-->>GW: Response
        GW-->>A1: Deliver Response
    else Trust Score Degraded
        PE->>GW: Restrict or Deny
        GW-->>A1: Communication Blocked
    end
    PE->>AL: Log Trust Decision
    GW->>AL: Log Interaction Details
```

## Trust Evaluation Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Collect[Context Collection]
        R[RACF Permissions]
        W[Workload Class]
        D[Data Sensitivity]
        A[Runtime Attestation]
    end

    subgraph Score[Trust Scoring]
        ID[Identity Validation]
        AZ[Authorization Check]
        ENV[Environment Verification]
        STATE[Operational State Check]
    end

    subgraph Decision[Trust Decision]
        CALC[Composite Trust Score]
        THRESH[Threshold Evaluation]
    end

    subgraph Outcome[Enforcement Outcome]
        PASS[Allow Per-Interaction Trust]
        LIMIT[Restrict Communication]
        BLOCK[Quarantine or Deny]
    end

    R & W & D & A --> ID
    R & W & D & A --> AZ
    R & W & D & A --> ENV
    R & W & D & A --> STATE
    ID & AZ & ENV & STATE --> CALC
    CALC --> THRESH
    THRESH -->|High Trust| PASS
    THRESH -->|Degraded Trust| LIMIT
    THRESH -->|Anomalous| BLOCK
```

## Continuous Re-Evaluation Lifecycle

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> RequestReceived
    RequestReceived --> ContextGathering
    ContextGathering --> ChallengeIssued
    ChallengeIssued --> TrustScored
    TrustScored --> Trusted: Score Above Threshold
    TrustScored --> Restricted: Score Marginal
    TrustScored --> Denied: Score Below Minimum
    Trusted --> InteractionActive
    Restricted --> InteractionLimited
    InteractionActive --> ReEvaluation: Continuous Monitoring
    InteractionLimited --> ReEvaluation
    ReEvaluation --> TrustScored: New Attestation
    Denied --> Quarantined
    Quarantined --> [*]
    ReEvaluation --> Denied: Anomaly Detected
```

TASK: Create mermaid.js diagrams for this invention. INSTRUCTION: Output ONLY mermaid code blocks. No explanations. MERMAID RULES (for PNG / mermaid-cli compatibility): - Do NOT use HTML line breaks in the diagram: no
,
, or similar anywhere in the mermaid source (including inside node labels). They break many renderers and image export. - Use shorter labels, multiple nodes, or subgraphs instead of forcing line breaks inside one label. INVENTION: --- invention-id: invention-20260622-110511 company: IBM created: 2026-06-22T11:05:17 --- # Invention Idea As autonomous agents become deployed across mainframe environments, trust is often inherited from the surrounding infrastructure rather than continuously validated. We propose a Zero-Trust Agent Fabric that governs all agent-to-agent communication within the mainframe, regardless of whether agents execute in LPARs, containers, address spaces, or AI accelerator domains. Before an agent can invoke another agent, the fabric evaluates security context derived from RACF permissions, workload classifications, data sensitivity labels, and runtime attestations. Rather than relying solely on static credentials, the fabric dynamically issues security challenges that validate an agent's current identity, authorization, execution environment, and operational state. Trust is therefore established per interaction and continuously re-evaluated as agents perform work. The system can automatically restrict, quarantine, or deny communications when trust scores degrade or anomalous behavior is detected. This creates a mainframe-native zero-trust architecture for autonomous agents that reduces lateral movement risks while providing a complete audit trail of agent trust decisions and interactions. OUTPUT: ## System Architecture `mermaid flowchart TD subgraph Input[Data Sources] A[Source A] B[Source B] end subgraph Process[Processing] C[Tracker] D[Detector] end subgraph Output[Results] E[Clean Data] F[Alerts] end A --> C B --> C C --> D D --> E D --> F ` ## Sequence Diagram `mermaid sequenceDiagram participant S as Source participant T as Tracker participant D as Detector participant Sys as System S->>T: Submit Data T->>D: Validate D->>Sys: Forward or Block ` Create diagrams specific to THIS invention.
